James D. Calhoun may be appointed deputy collector of customs at
the Port of Tampa, in the District of Florida, in the State of Florida,
under the reorganization of the Customs Service which becomes effective
July I st, 1913, without compliance with the civil service rules.
The Civil Service Commission concurs with the Secretary of the
Treasury in recommending the issuance of this order. The Collector is
required to spend the larger part of his time at Jacksonville, the desig-
nated headquarters, and it is necessary to put deputies in charge of the
other ports in the State. The Secretary of the Treasury states that he is
not satisfied that any of the deputies in Florida are sufficiently competent
to be entrusted with the management of the important port of Tampa
where the collections amount to $1,867,763.84 per annum, which is more
than three times that of the next largest port in the State.
A number of temporary appointments have been made in the Florida
collection district without examination because of the lack of eligibles.
The number of eligibles in that district for positions of this character has
been insufficient, both in number and in the grades obtained in examina-
tion, to meet the needs of the service.
WOODROW WILSON
THlE WRITE HOUSE,
3 Jul1y, 1913.
[No. '795.1

In accordance with the provisions of section 40 of the act entitled
"An act to increase the efficiency of the permanent military establishment
of the United States", approved February 2, 1901, which authorizes the
President to "prescribe the kinds and quantities of the component articles
of the Army ration, and to direct the issue of substitutive equivalent articles
in place of any such components whenever, in his opinion, economy and
a due regard to the health and comfort of the troops may so require," the
Executive Order of January 21, 1913, is amended as follows:
The authority for the addition of lard compound as a substitutive
article for lard in the garrison ration is revoked, and the following
authorized instead:
"Garrison Ration.
Lard substitute is added as a substitutive article for lard, at the
rate of .64 oz. to the ration."
WOODROW WILSON
THE WHITE HOUSE,
July '5, 1913.

T, Woodrow Wilson, President of the United States, by virtue of the
authority vested in me by Section 3141 of the Revised Statutes of the
United States, hereby order that the counties of Guilford, Randolph and
Rockingham, now a part of the Fourth Internal Revenue Collection Dis-
trict of North Carolina, be transferred to and made a part of the Fifth
Internal Revenue Collection District of North Carolina.
This order to take effect on the First day of November, 1913.
WOODROW WILSON
THE WHITE HOUSE,
29 October, 1913.
[No. 1850.E

It is hereby ordered that whenever new structures are to be erected
in the District of Columbia under the direction of the federal government
which affect in any important way the appearance of the City, or when-
ever questions involving matters of art and with which the federal govern-
ment is concerned are to be determined, final action shall not be taken
until such plans and questions have been submitted to the Commissioners
of Fine Arts designated under the Act of Congress of May 17, 1910, for
their comment and advice.
